topic: ICSE 10th Board Section A - Part 1: Multiple Choice Questions (Marks: 20)

questions.question: Which of the following data types occupies exactly 1 byte in memory?
questions.explanation: In Java, the primitive type 'byte' is an 8-bit signed two's complement integer, occupying exactly 1 byte.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Character.isDigit('7')?
questions.explanation: Character validation methods starting with 'is' (such as isDigit, isLetter) return a primitive boolean value.

questions.question: Which operator performs shorthand addition and assignment in Java?
questions.explanation: '+=' is the compound assignment operator that adds the right-hand operand to the left-hand variable and reassigns the result.

questions.question: What is the result of Math.abs(15.7)?
questions.explanation: Math.abs() returns the absolute magnitude without alteration if the input value is already positive.

questions.question: Which access specifier allows member access within the same package and by subclasses in other packages?
questions.explanation: The 'protected' access modifier grants visibility to package members as well as derived subclasses across packages.

questions.question: What is the output of 22 % 7?
questions.explanation: 22 divided by 7 equals 3 with a remainder of 1; the modulus operator '%' extracts this remainder.

questions.question: What will "APPLICATION".indexOf('P') return?
questions.explanation: indexOf() scans from left to right and reports the index of the first matched occurrence: 'A'(0), 'P'(1).

questions.question: Which term describes a function that does not alter any instance variables or external data?
questions.explanation: A pure function (accessor) accesses and returns values without mutating the state of the object or its arguments[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which escape character represents a newline in Java console output?
questions.explanation: '\n' advances the console cursor directly to the beginning of the next line.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method s.endsWith(".java") on a String s?
questions.explanation: Suffix-checking methods in String verify matching endings and return true or false.

questions.question: Which keyword prevents an instantiated variable's value from being modified later?
questions.explanation: Declaring a primitive or reference variable with 'final' locks its value and prevents reassignment.

questions.question: What will Math.max(-10, -50) evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Math.max() returns the larger number; -10 is algebraically greater than -50.

questions.question: What does the expression (char)('a' - 32) produce in Java?
questions.explanation: The ASCII value of 'a' is 97. 97 - 32 = 65, which corresponds to character literal 'A' when cast back to char.

questions.question: Which loop evaluation occurs strictly at the entry point prior to any body execution?
questions.explanation: Both 'while' and 'for' are entry-controlled loops because their test conditions are checked prior to loop entry.

questions.question: Which Wrapper class method converts a primitive integer to its textual String representation?
questions.explanation: Integer.toString(int i) converts primitive numerical integers directly into String representations.

questions.question: What is the default initial element value when creating a new String[] of size 5?
questions.explanation: Arrays of reference types (like String) automatically populate vacant slots with 'null' references.

questions.question: What is the return value of Math.rint(3.5)?
questions.explanation: Math.rint() rounds to the nearest mathematical integer; equidistant half-values round toward the nearest even integer (4.0).

questions.question: Which mechanism describes passing a copy of the actual argument's value into method parameters?
questions.explanation: Java strictly uses call-by-value, creating and supplying duplicate values for primitive formal parameters.

questions.question: Which logical operator short-circuits evaluation when the first operand evaluates to false?
questions.explanation: The conditional-AND operator '&&' skips evaluating second arguments whenever the initial expression resolves to false.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method "ICSE".toLowerCase()?
questions.explanation: toLowerCase() creates and returns an entirely new transformed String instance.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this character assignment:
options: char data type cannot hold multiple characters in single quotes
ch is an illegal variable identifier
questions.answer: char data type cannot hold multiple characters in single quotes
questions.explanation: A char literal stores exactly one 16-bit Unicode character; multi-letter literals must be enclosed in double quotes as Strings[cite: 2].

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this 2D Array allocation:
options: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [3][3], not parentheses (3)(3)
questions.answer: Array dimension capacity must be specified using square brackets [3][3], not parentheses (3)(3)
questions.explanation: Multidimensional arrays in Java strictly use square bracket pairs to indicate sizing and dimensions[cite: 1, 2].

questions.question: Identify the logical flaw in this countdown loop:
options: i++ increments instead of decrementing (i--), causing an infinite loop
questions.answer: i++ increments instead of decrementing (i--), causing an infinite loop
questions.explanation: Incrementing i moves it further above 1, keeping the condition i >= 1 permanently true and triggering an infinite loop.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
questions.code_snippet:
String msg = "Hello World";
int len = msg.length;
options: String uses the method length(), not the field property length
questions.answer: String uses the method length(), not the field property length
questions.explanation: Arrays use the length field property, whereas String objects require the invocation of length() with parentheses[cite: 1].

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this conditional equality check:
options: Comparison requires equality operator '==', not assignment '='
if condition must end with a semicolon
questions.answer: Comparison requires equality operator '==', not assignment '='
questions.explanation: A single '=' attempts value assignment inside the if condition, which is invalid since it evaluates to an integer rather than a boolean[cite: 1].

questions.question: Identify the logical error in this range-checking condition for positive numbers up to 100:
options: Requires logical AND (&&) instead of OR (||); current logic is unconditionally true for all numbers
questions.answer: Requires logical AND (&&) instead of OR (||); current logic is unconditionally true for all numbers
questions.explanation: Using OR (||) causes the check to match every possible number because any number is either greater than 0 or less than 100.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
options: Method name must follow camelCase: valueOf()
questions.answer: Method name must follow camelCase: valueOf()
questions.explanation: Java methods strictly enforce camelCase naming; the correct method call is Integer.valueOf()[cite: 1].

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this method signature:
options: Every formal parameter must specify its own explicit data type (int a, int b)
questions.answer: Every formal parameter must specify its own explicit data type (int a, int b)
questions.explanation: In Java method parameter lists, each variable must be declared with its own individual type specifier.

questions.explanation: Math.ceil(2.2) rounds up to 3.0. Math.floor(2.8) rounds down to 2.0. Adding them yields 5.0[cite: 1].
